title: X Feed Digest
summary: Codex shipped the highest-signal product updates in the batch: Appshots, locked-Mac remote control, goal mode GA, and CLI lifecycle hooks that make agent workflows less brittle.
Google spent the day in damage control around Antigravity, tripling Gemini limits and resetting quotas after users pushed back hard on paid-tier caps.

The AI labor-market conversation turned sharper: both ClickUp and Meta framed leaner staffing as compatible with strong business performance, with value shifting toward orchestrators, reviewers, and customer-facing humans.
Markets chatter kept extending the AI capex story beyond training clusters, with Nvidia bulls already rotating toward on-device AI, hybrid edge/cloud deployments, and physical-AI follow-ons.
The most thoughtful builder posts agreed on the next bottleneck: not raw model IQ, but context handoff, coordination, and review across humans plus multiple agents.

items.title: @Codex_Changelog: Appshots and Locked-Mac Control
items.body: OpenAI’s latest Codex app update bundled the most immediately useful product changes: Appshots for pulling a live app window into a thread, goal mode graduating out of beta, and remote computer use even after a Mac locks. The practical signal is that Codex is moving from chat assistant toward a persistent operator that can keep working against real UI context.

items.title: @Codex_Changelog: CLI 0.133.0 for Agent Workflows
items.body: Codex CLI 0.133.0 turned goals on by default and added dedicated storage, plugin inventory tooling, and lifecycle events for subagents, tools, and turns. Those sound small, but they directly reduce glue-code pain for people building repeatable agent workflows instead of one-off prompts.

items.title: @_mohansolo: Antigravity Triples Gemini Limits
items.body: Varun Mohan said Antigravity is tripling Gemini rate limits across all paid tiers and resetting weekly quotas after users ran into caps almost immediately. The bigger takeaway is that AI coding products are now being judged like infrastructure: if throughput feels fake or cramped, users revolt fast.

items.title: @elvissun: What a Long /goal Run Actually Costs
items.body: Elvis shared a live Codex /goal run that wrote roughly 6,300 lines while consuming only a few dollars of external model and scraping spend, plus 14% of a weekly Codex quota. More useful than the flex was the lesson: goal-oriented agent prompts need a different shape than classic spec-driven coding prompts.

items.title: @GergelyOrosz: Meta Layoffs Despite Record Profits
items.body: Gergely Orosz highlighted the dissonance of Meta cutting 10% of staff while revenue growth and profits are near highs, arguing the move looks more like executive choice than financial necessity. For anyone watching tech employment or margins, that is a blunt reminder that AI-era cost discipline can show up even when the business is healthy.

items.title: @DJ_CURFEW: ClickUp’s '100x Organization' Bet
items.body: ClickUp’s CEO said the company cut 22% of headcount from a position of strength because AI is changing which roles create leverage, with more value concentrating in people who can orchestrate and review agent output. Whether you agree or not, it was one of the clearest first-person statements in the batch about how management teams are re-architecting org charts around AI productivity.

items.title: @Leooo2099: Nvidia Bulls Extend the AI Capex Story
items.body: A widely shared Nvidia thesis argued the next leg is moving from datacenter training toward AI PCs, AI phones, and hybrid local-plus-cloud deployments, while physical AI remains earlier still. The market read is that investors are already looking for second-order beneficiaries beyond the obvious chip winners.

items.title: @spolu: Multiplayer AI, Not Solo Copilots
items.body: Dust’s CEO argued that as agents stretch from minutes of work to days or weeks, the real architecture shift is toward shared context, handoffs, and multiple humans steering multiple agents together. The funding announcement mattered less than the framing: coordination is emerging as the next bottleneck for enterprise AI.

items.title: @stanine: Compliance Automation Moves Into the Core Stack
items.body: Rippling launched Automated Compliance starting with SOC 2, pitching the advantage of already owning device, identity, HR, and performance data instead of sitting beside the stack as a checklist tool. That is a useful enterprise pattern to watch: boring admin workflows are getting automated fastest where the system of record is already in place.

items.title: @MaxForAI: Google’s Product Maze Is Becoming the Product
items.body: A sharply observed post mapped Google’s growing AI naming maze across Gemini, AI Studio, Antigravity, Jules, Flow/Veo, AI Mode, and NotebookLM. It landed because it captures a real adoption problem: even strong models lose momentum when the entry points feel fragmented and bureaucratic.
